title: First Sounds & Signals
intro: Babies don't start language learning with grammar rules or text books — they learn by associating sounds directly with intent, feelings, and physical gestures. Today we anchor your first 3 core Kannada sounds.

words.babyAnalogy: The universal first smile and wave when acknowledging someone.
words.actionTag: Say 'Namaskara' to your security guard, vendor, or colleague today instead of 'Hi'.

words.babyAnalogy: The enthusiastic head nod when accepting food or agreeing.
words.actionTag: Nod and say 'Haudu' whenever you mean 'Yes' today.

words.babyAnalogy: The head shake when refusing food or pointing to an empty bowl.
words.actionTag: Say 'Illa' when an auto driver offers a ride you don't need or when something is unavailable.

combos.context: Ideal morning greeting to start any interaction.
Direct polite refusal or stating absence.

quiz.scenario: You bump into your landlord or neighbor in the hallway.
quiz.question: What is the respectful sound to greet them?
quiz.explanation: Namaskara (ನಮಸ್ಕಾರ) is the respectful universal greeting in Kannada.
